verdict.rationale: PostHog's experiments docs say results are read 'with significance' over funnel, mean, or ratio metrics, so the product does ship a statistical layer behind its experiment results. The evidence never names the methodology or any variance-reduction technique, so trust in a documented engine is only thinly supported. Missing for 10: documentation of Bayesian vs frequentist methodology, variance-reduction options (e.g. CUPED), statistical-engine docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can trust a documented statistics engine (Bayesian or frequentist, with variance-reduction options) behind experiment results

citations.quote: Create experiments, launch them, and read results with significance, replays, and exposures in view.
Any event you already capture can become a funnel, mean, or ratio metric for an experiment.
